text:
### Observed differences

- Participation: A27, A36, A37 and A42 were each present in only about 47–55 in 100 traces in the earlier window (at most once per trace); in the later window each is present in essentially every trace (about 995–1,000 in 1,000), still about once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
- A27 and the trio A36/A37/A42 were alternatives before: they co-occurred in only about 1 in 100 traces. In the later window they run together in about 995 in 1,000 traces, with the trio executed before A27 in about 96–97 in 100. [REL011, REL012, REL013]
- The trio itself kept its unfixed internal order but became mandatory: the three ran together in about 46 in 100 traces before and about 995 in 1,000 after, with both orders in similar shares in each window. [REL020, REL021, REL022]
- Routing at A26 collapsed to one target: earlier its outgoing transitions went to A27 in 54% of cases and to A36/A37/A42 in about 45% combined; in the later window 98% go to A27. [DIR002]
- Routing at A25 changed: earlier 97% of A25's outgoing transitions led to A28; later about 96% lead to the trio (roughly a third each to A36, A37, A42) and under 1% to A28. [DIR001]
- The trio's exit moved: earlier A36, A37 and A42 each led to A31 in about 29–39% of their outgoing transitions; later each leads to A28 in about 31–35%, and A31 is no longer a successor of the trio. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Order reversals around the trio: earlier A26 preceded the trio in about 46 in 100 of their joint traces, while later the trio precedes A26 in about 98–99 in 100; similarly, A28 preceded the trio in about 46 in 100 before, and the trio precedes A28 in about 97–99 in 100 after. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- Distances match this rearrangement: A28 followed A25 within one step in 96 in 100 earlier cases but 4–5 steps later in 99 in 100 later cases; A31 followed A26 two steps later in 54% and four steps in 42% of earlier cases, and consistently two steps (97%) in the later window. [LAG001, LAG003]
- Mean event positions shifted accordingly: the trio from about 0.59 to about 0.41, A28 from 0.40 to 0.46, A26 from 0.54 to 0.60, A27 from 0.58 to 0.63 (event positions, not clock time). [POS006, POS007, POS008, POS004, POS002, POS003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the either/or branch after A26 was removed and the segment A36/A37/A42 became a mandatory block placed between A25 and A28, while A27 became a mandatory step between A26 and A31. Earlier, a case ran A25, immediately followed by A28, and A26 then routed either to A27 (about 55 in 100 cases) or to the trio in varying internal order (about 45 in 100), with both alternatives preceding A31, which appeared in every trace; in the later window every case runs A25, then the trio in no fixed order, then A28 (whose mean position, about 0.46, now lies before A26's, about 0.60), then A26 and A27, again ending before A31. [REL011, REL012, REL013, REL010, REL017, REL018, REL019, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, POS005]

The change is shown directly by relational evidence (co-occurrence rising from about 1 in 100 to about 995 in 1,000, and order reversals), by successor changes at A25, A26 and the trio, and by the participation increase, with the distance changes consistent throughout; 48 control-flow items qualified against roughly 0.74 expected if nothing had changed, so chance cannot account for the set as a whole. [REL006, REL011, REL014, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, OCC001, LAG001, LAG003]

An important competing explanation remains: the evidence cannot show whether the earlier either/or pattern was a routing choice inside one process or two coexisting case variants, so a replacement of the case mix cannot be ruled out. Several lag items (LAG002, LAG004–LAG009) rest on only 1–2 observations on one side and were not used in this judgement. [REL011, LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]
